claims.text: For noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles containing at least five elements, crystal-structure selection under rapid thermal processing is governed by competition between stochastic alloy formation and limited atomic mobility.
Rapid heating uniformly disperses the constituent elements.
Ultra-fast cooling can kinetically trap a single-phase solid solution by suppressing diffusion and secondary-phase formation.
Reducing the cooling rate while holding peak temperature and dwell time constant increases atomic mobility.
The increased mobility produced by slower cooling allows preferential elemental interactions and local ordering to cause phase separation and elemental segregation.
Atomic mobility is limited when a mixed solid precursor is reduced under the relevant synthesis conditions.
The spatial distribution and density of local nucleation centers formed during reduction determine whether random alloying or local ordering and phase separation occur.
Increasing the number of element types promotes formation of a more random alloy when free atomic mobility is limited.
Distinct elemental mixing enthalpies create preferences for particular structures that are opposed by limited atomic mobility.
At a cooling rate of approximately 10^5 K/s, the baseline nanoparticles should form a kinetically trapped single-phase solid solution.
Progressively slower cooling should produce phase separation, elemental segregation, or ordered secondary phases relative to the ultra-fast-cooled baseline.
The structural response to decreasing cooling rate should be gradual.
A system-specific critical cooling rate exists below which phase separation becomes evident.
The approximate critical cooling-rate boundary is below 10^4 K/s.
The proposed mechanism applies to fixed-composition systems containing at least five noble-metal elements and starting from uniformly mixed solid precursors.
The critical cooling rate depends on elemental mixing enthalpies and precursor microstructure or distribution.
If cooling below the predicted threshold produces no measurable structural or compositional difference from the ultra-fast-cooled control, the proposed cooling-rate mechanism is falsified.
